thread:
incident-bot: [P0] GPU pressure spike — single-tenant dedicated pool (ZenithCorp) > 95% GPU utilization for 6m, backpressure rising, errors on customer requests. Paging oncall.
maria-sre: ack. I'm on it, pulling metrics and logs.
maria-sre: nvidia-smi from node-gpu-12 shows repeated long-running processes from zenith-rt worker group.
```
Fri Mar 17 12:02:11 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 520.61.05    Driver Version: 520.61.05    CUDA Version: 11.8 |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M|Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-SXM4-40G     Off        00000000:00:1E.0  N/A   0              |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
| GPU   PID   Type   Process name                             GPU Mem Usage    |
| 0    23456  C     zenith-rt --model=llama-70b                       36000MiB |
| 0    23500  C     zenith-batch-processor                            4000MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

jay-runtime: looks like a few persistent 70B model workers are hogging KV caches. Are those pinned to the dedicated pool? (cc @amelia-cs)
amelia-cs: yes, ZenithCorp requested single-tenant residency for compliance. They run latency-critical pipelines. I've pinged the customer but no response yet.
sam-ops: we have two levers: emergency-burst to shared burst capacity (if allowed by contract) or evict/rotate low-priority jobs. Which should we do? Need approval from product infra for burst.
maria-sre: quick impact: API error rate up 12% for Zenith since 11:57, tail latency > 10s. No cross-tenant impact yet but risk of spillover. I recommend temporary burst + soft-throttle of long-running jobs.
jay-runtime: policy check: Zenith's Dedicated SLA allows 30 minutes of burst to shared-pool with CS signoff. Amelia — can you confirm customer-level approval remotely, or do we proceed with emergency auto-burst under incident playbook?
amelia-cs: I cannot reach the primary contact. Per contract, we have emergency permission for transient burst under 'operational continuity' clause, but we must notify them within 1h. I'll send the notification now and post the message I send.
amelia-cs: "ZenithCorp ops — we detected sustained GPU pressure in your dedicated pool. We're enabling a transient burst to keep your service healthy for up to 30 minutes; expect a short re-route of some background workloads. Please reply if you object." (sent)
lee-eng: parallel mitigation: can we flip some Zenith traffic to a quantized 8-bit variant of the model? Quality loss expected but reduces GPU by ~40% for streaming workloads.
maria-sre: yes, we have a canary route ready. Plan: 1) enable emergency-burst (owner: jay-runtime) 2) throttle batch/worker jobs to free 2+ GPUs (owner: sam-ops) 3) route subset (10%) to quantized model as graceful degradation (owner: lee-eng) 4) CS notification (owner: amelia-cs) 5) create incident page and track postmortem (owner: maria-sre).
sam-ops: starting throttle now: scaling batch workers from 12 -> 4 for zenith-batch-processor. Running command:
```
kubectl scale deployment/zenith-batch-processor --replicas=4 -n dedicated-zenith
```
maria-sre: throttle in effect, freeing ~8GB*2 GPUs within 90s. Monitoring.
jay-runtime: requesting emergency-burst via infra API now. If approved, we'll attach 4 shared GPUs from regional burst pool for 30m. Command:
```
POST /infra/burst-requests {"tenant":"zenith","gpus":4,"duration_min":30,"reason":"dedicated pool pressure"}
```
incident-bot: burst request created (id br-10087) — pending manual approve by infra-lead. Notifying infra-lead.
lee-eng: enabling 10% routing to quantized model: set feature flag rollout 10%.
```
redwood-ff set zenith-quant-rollout --percent=10 --env=prod
```
maria-sre: metrics after throttle & 10% quant route: GPU pressure down to 81% in 2m, error rate falling. Good signs.
amelia-cs: customer acked — "Thanks, give us a heads up if you need >30m." They have no objection to short reroute.
jay-runtime: infra-lead approved br-10087. Attaching 4 shared GPUs now.
incident-bot: burst br-10087: attached 4 GPUs from regional pool. Pool remaining capacity: 12 GPUs.
maria-sre: after attaching burst, GPU utilization at 62%, tail latency back to SLO. Monitoring for degradation or eviction side-effects.
sam-ops: continuing to drain long jobs; will resume normal replicas in 35m. Logged action in runbook.
lee-eng: scheduling canary rollback to 0% quant if quality alerts fire. Also prepared a model-variant fallback if we hit memory contention.
amelia-cs: I've updated ZenithCorp with the actions taken and ETA for return to normal. They asked for a short status call if we need >30m.
maria-sre: creating incident page and assigning postmortem owners. Incident page: https://incidents.redwood/1002345678
maria-sre: handoff — I'm going to document everything and hand this to jay-runtime as the incident transitions. Jay, you'll own monitoring until burst expires at +30m unless we extend.
jay-runtime: taking handoff. Will short-check in at +15m and extend only with CS consent. Thanks team :thumbsup:
incident-bot: incident status changed -> mitigation in place. Next update scheduled in 15m.
